source_scope: Diseases of Swine, 11th Edition, pages 201-400 markdown extraction
note: These are paraphrased operational facts derived from pages 201-400. They should be reviewed before insertion into exports/knowledge_facts.json.

candidate_facts.subject: swine disease QA procedural content
candidate_facts.object: Detailed anesthesia, epidural, surgery, castration, prolapse, hernia, or amputation content should be used as safety context and complication differentials, not as train-ready executable protocols.

candidate_facts.subject: preharvest swine medicine
candidate_facts.object: Swine treatment and handling decisions can affect human health through physical hazards, chemical residues, biological hazards, occupational exposure, environmental exposure, and antimicrobial resistance.

candidate_facts.subject: broken needle event
candidate_facts.object: Broken needle risk should be managed through proper restraint, needle selection, injection technique, worker education, suspect-animal identification, and communication with the processor.

candidate_facts.subject: swine-associated zoonotic risk
candidate_facts.object: Swine-associated human-health risks include foodborne hazards from pork and non-foodborne risks from direct occupational, show, pet, and environmental exposures.

candidate_facts.subject: show pigs
candidate_facts.object: Show-pig cases should consider movement, commingling, exhibition stress, transport, human contact, and event drug-testing or ethics boundaries.

candidate_facts.subject: swine sudden death cyanosis pallor edema or ascites
candidate_facts.object: Sudden death, cyanosis, pallor, edema, ascites, shock, poor growth, and exercise intolerance should trigger cardiovascular and hematopoietic differentials in addition to infectious disease differentials.

candidate_facts.subject: swine anemia
candidate_facts.object: Anemia should be differentiated by defective erythropoiesis, hemolysis, hemorrhage, and hemoglobin-related disorders rather than treated as a single diagnosis.

candidate_facts.subject: swine diarrhea
candidate_facts.object: Swine diarrhea differentials should consider age, hypersecretion, malabsorption, inflammation, permeability, hemorrhage, ulceration, obstruction, torsion, and lesion distribution.

candidate_facts.subject: endemic enteric agent detection
candidate_facts.object: Culture, PCR, or metagenomic detection of common endemic enteric agents is not sufficient for definitive causation without compatible history, clinical signs, and gross or microscopic lesions.

candidate_facts.subject: neonatal piglet diarrhea
candidate_facts.object: Neonatal piglet diarrhea differentials include E. coli, rotavirus, clostridial disease, Cystoisospora, cryptosporidia, coronaviruses, and noninfectious risk factors; diagnosis should match age, lesions, and tests.

candidate_facts.subject: hemorrhagic enteric signs
candidate_facts.object: Mucohemorrhagic diarrhea, melena, fresh blood clots, or sudden death with dark distended intestines should trigger differentials such as Lawsonia, Brachyspira, Salmonella, gastric ulcer, Trichuris, clostridial disease, torsion, hemorrhagic bowel syndrome, poisoning, CSF, and ASF.

candidate_facts.subject: mixed enteric infections
candidate_facts.object: Mixed enteric infections and nonspecific colitis require histopathology or tissue localization to confirm the pathologic role of detected agents.

candidate_facts.subject: serious epidemic disease with enteric signs
candidate_facts.object: When CSF or ASF are plausible in enteric or hemorrhagic disease, answers should prioritize reporting and rapid investigation rather than routine diarrhea treatment.

candidate_facts.subject: newborn piglet immunity
candidate_facts.object: Newborn piglet disease risk should consider colostrum intake, passive transfer, small or late-born piglets, teat access, sow lactation, and early management.

candidate_facts.subject: swine vaccine failure
candidate_facts.object: Vaccine failure should be evaluated for maternal antibody interference, timing, storage, administration route, antigen match, herd immunity, challenge pressure, immunosuppression, nutrition, and coinfections.

candidate_facts.subject: autogenous vaccines and planned exposure
candidate_facts.object: Autogenous vaccines and planned exposure should not be generated as casual recommendations; they require veterinary, biosecurity, welfare, and regulatory review.

candidate_facts.subject: swine skin disease
candidate_facts.object: Skin disease workup should record lesion type, distribution, age, environment, pruritus, pain, crusts, vesicles, ulcers, necrosis, and choose biopsy, scraping/direct examination, culture, or PCR as appropriate.

candidate_facts.subject: swine skin lesions
candidate_facts.object: Swine skin lesions can involve bacterial, viral, fungal, parasitic, environmental, nutritional, congenital, hoof/claw, and reportable vesicular or hemorrhagic disease differentials.

candidate_facts.subject: weak neonatal piglets
candidate_facts.object: Weak neonatal piglets, poor early growth, or neonatal disease clusters should consider colostrum intake, teat access, sow milk production, and mammary health in addition to infectious disease.

candidate_facts.subject: postpartum dysgalactia syndrome
candidate_facts.object: PDS and mastitis evaluation should include sow signs, udder findings, piglet behavior, farrowing context, environment, nutrition, water availability, and management.

candidate_facts.subject: swine neurologic signs
candidate_facts.object: Neurologic cases should localize the problem to forebrain, cerebellum, spinal cord, vestibular/eye, peripheral nerve, muscle, bone, or joint before assigning a final disease label.

candidate_facts.subject: neurologic and locomotor sampling
candidate_facts.object: Antemortem and postmortem samples for neurologic and locomotor problems should be selected according to clinical localization, lesion distribution, safety, and zoonotic or reportable-disease risk.

candidate_facts.subject: swine lameness
candidate_facts.object: Lameness should distinguish bone, joint, muscle, hoof/claw, fracture, osteochondrosis, infectious arthritis, polyarthritis, nutritional myopathy, and sow or boar locomotor disorders.

candidate_facts.subject: swine reproductive failure
candidate_facts.object: Reproductive failure should be framed with herd-level records, parity distribution, puberty, weaning-to-estrus interval, conception and farrowing rates, returns, abortion timing, stillbirths, mummification, and individual sow or gilt examination.
